system.summary: Plain Chinese standard telegraph code (four-digit codes), no encipherment, read in typing order. (The Dalai Lama's replies in the same file, pp. 9, 11, 12, 22-23, are in pronounceable 5-letter code words, CVCVC and VCVCV joined in pairs, probably from a codebook; they are not part of this reading: see NOTES.md and outcome.gaps.)
system.notes: Date codes (韻目): 元 = 13th, 庚 = 8th.

prior_solution.where: Foreign and Political Department to Weir, D.O. 29 Sept 1930 (same file p. 18): an English abstract of the Nanking messages (Chiang received the Dalai Lama's letter through Kun Kanpu; China had not been 'honest or considerate'; complete unity; greetings from Ma Fuxiang and Kun Kanpu). Lead 1359 (Daniel Bourdeau): open, CTC 'not tested further' (vetting of 11 Nov 2026). Web search 11 Nov 2026: nothing printed.

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout chose the target, logged in to Abhilekh Patal and captured the pages, and set the rules (protocol hashed before the attack; every decipherment goes to Daniel). A Claude Opus 5.5 agent checked the groups, wrote the protocol, read the telegrams, ran the controls and wrote up.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agent run by Brice Dudout (protocol, reading, controls, write-up)

solution.what: File seen after login on Abhilekh Patal (NAIDLF03824535); pp. 9-23 captured; OCR text layer of pp. 9-15 read.
Lead 1359 status (open); web search on the 1930 Nanking-Lhasa telegrams: nothing printed.

Protocol hashed before the attack (frozen/PREREG.md, SHA-256 23aba69b...): plain standard telegraph code first; additives and the 1908 General Staff formula held in reserve. Plain code worked at once on pp. 14-15.

Crib words of two or more characters fixed in the protocol: 14 (p. 14) and 10 (p. 15) against max 4 and 3 over 1,000 random orders of the groups; 1,000 random 4-digit additives max 2 (frozen/controles_A.out). Both halves of each telegram read.
p. 14: 150 certain + 3 probable (one-digit slips) + 2 unresolved of 155; p. 15: 71 + 3 + 1 of 75.

Code words (pp. 9, 11, 12): structure found (5-letter words CVCVC/VCVCV, shared opening and closing words between pp. 11 and 12). A syllable-to-digit-pair table (word = CTC number + filler letter), tried with the guess that the shared closing words spell 達賴喇嘛, is inconsistent; alphabetical rank of the words gives nothing. No crib (the p. 18 abstract covers the Nanking telegrams, not these). The held-out message (p. 9), designated in the protocol, was never used: no key, no measurement.

outcome.method_basis: The key is the public Chinese standard telegraph code (table from Unicode Unihan); the telegrams are not enciphered.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Nanking telegrams: p. 14 153 of 155 codes read by sense (150 certain + 3 probable), p. 15 74 of 75 (71 + 3); 227/230 = 98.7%. The code-word telegrams (pp. 9, 11, 12, 22-23) are not read and not counted.

texts.label: p. 14: Chiang Kai-shek to the Dalai Lama, September 1930 (the 13th)
texts.summary: Chiang Kai-shek thanks the Dalai Lama for the letter, replies on eight points, photograph and gifts brought by Kun Kanpu; admits that past rulers did not treat Tibet with sincerity; welcomes his support of the central government; China and Tibet one family, unification completed; Ma Fuxiang instructed to handle the matter.

reading_review.by: Claude Opus 5.5 agent for Brice Dudout
reading_review.note: Read as Chinese official telegram prose (wenyan): opening on Kun Kanpu's audience, polite formulas, closing 並祝健康, signature 蔣中正 and date code 元; every point of the British abstract of 1930 is in it. 150 codes give the character directly, 3 one-digit slips emended, 2 unresolved. No human sinologist has re-read it.

texts.label: p. 15: Ma Fuxiang to the Dalai Lama, September 1930 (the 8th)
texts.summary: Ma Fuxiang, after twenty years apart, has met Kun Kanpu; Chiang praises the Dalai Lama's support and has answered by telegram; Ma will handle his affairs with devotion.

reading_review.by: Claude Opus 5.5 agent for Brice Dudout
reading_review.note: Read as Chinese letter-telegram prose: 暌違廿餘載 opening, 敬祝嘉福 closing, signature 馬福祥, date code 庚. 71 codes direct, 3 one-digit slips emended, 1 unresolved. No human sinologist has re-read it.

outcome.notes: No image of the NAI file is included (no reuse licence shown). Not a first break: the Government of India summarised these two telegrams in 1930. New here: the Chinese texts and translations. The Dalai Lama's code-word replies in the same file remain unread.
